edges.description: With no transferrin to bind absorbed iron, plasma iron circulates as reactive non-transferrin-bound iron.
Loss of transferrin removes a positive input to hepatic hepcidin expression, lowering hepcidin.

edges.description: The mechanism manifests clinically and on laboratory testing as anemia.
Chronic anemia in infancy impairs growth.
Non-transferrin-bound iron is taken up unregulated by parenchymal cells, depositing as tissue hemosiderosis.
Low hepcidin de-represses intestinal iron absorption and ferroportin-mediated efflux, feeding the non-transferrin-bound iron pool.
Myocardial iron deposition produces iron-overload cardiomyopathy.
Chronic hepatic iron loading and oxidative injury drive fibrosis.
Progressive hepatic fibrosis advances to cirrhosis.
Pancreatic iron deposition impairs insulin secretion.
Thyroid iron deposition impairs thyroid hormone production.
Iron overload is associated with splenomegaly.
Tissue iron loading is reflected in elevated serum ferritin.
Iron deposits in the liver parenchyma.

nodes.description: Infusion of apotransferrin (purified or plasma-derived) or fresh-frozen plasma restores iron transport, corrects the anemia, and redistributes parenchymal iron. This is the disease-specific, mechanism-directed therapy.
